record.narrative: Because this is iteration 1 and there is no prior evidence, I propose a broad but feasible screening set focused on measured binary predictors and one common two-level nominal predictor. Binary predictors are preferred because group sizes are transparent from the supplied counts and most have at least 100 observations in the exposed or unexposed category, reducing the risk of failing the minimum 20 observations per comparison cell. I also prioritize outcomes with larger SD or unusual means, especially outcome_001, outcome_014, outcome_006, outcome_013, outcome_011, and outcome_008, because these appear to carry more outcome variability and may be more likely to reveal dependency heterogeneity. The negative-direction hypotheses represent stronger dependency in the exposed group, i.e. a raw exposed-minus-comparator mean difference that is more negative. The positive-direction hypotheses represent weaker dependency or possible resistance-like phenotype in the exposed group. Interaction hypotheses ask whether the effect of a ~20% prevalence marker is modified by a ~50% prevalence subgroup marker. I avoid continuous and poorly balanced categorical predictors in this first round because the controller may require cell-count safety and because nominal levels with sparse cells could be underpowered. The 10% relative-dependency rule is interpreted practically by outcome scale: for standard outcomes with means around -0.25, a signed clinical effect is near 0.025 in the claimed direction; for outcome_001 it is nearer 0.04; for outcome_014 and outcome_006, whose means are near zero, relative scaling is unstable, so I would judge those using a similar absolute shift around 0.025 rather than a literal 10% of a near-zero mean. These analyses are associational in the supplied dataset only; correlated predictors, confounding, and generalizability remain unresolved.

This is the first analysis request, so I am selecting all 12 registered claims for discovery evaluation. The set intentionally covers diverse CRISPR dependency outcomes and measured predictors, including common binary markers, one two-level categorical predictor, low-prevalence binary markers, and interaction hypotheses. Running all registered hypotheses now maximizes early information while remaining within the 12-comparison limit. No claims have evidence yet, so no status assessments can be changed in this analyze form.

No claim should be accepted yet. The estimates are already signed to the claimed direction, so positive values support the claim and negative values point away from it. I interpreted the 10% clinical threshold using the relevant comparator/overall mean magnitude: roughly 0.025 for outcomes centered near -0.25, about 0.041 for outcome_001, and about 0.009 for outcome_014/outcome_006 because their means are near zero. Because near-zero denominators make relative thresholds unstable, I also considered whether a roughly 0.02-0.025 absolute shift would be scientifically relevant on the dependency-score scale. None has a discovery interval that fully clears a clinically meaningful threshold, so no claim is accepted. H1, H4, H5, H6, and H7 are rejected because their intervals or estimates indicate effects well below the relevant clinical threshold. H11 is rejected for the claimed positive interaction because the point estimate is opposite the claimed direction and there is no positive evidence, despite a wide interval. H3, H8, H10, H2, H9, and H12 remain unresolved: they either include clinically meaningful values within the interval or are too imprecise to dismiss. I kept H3 and H10 active because their point estimates are promising but the uncertainty is too large to accept; H2, H9, and H12 are deferred because the point estimates are near null and follow-up would not be efficient now. H8 is the single validation target because it is a main effect on a standard-scale dependency outcome, has a near-significant positive signed effect close to the 10% clinical boundary, and is the most informative borderline claim for independent replication. I see no evidence of outcome leakage from the provided predictor coding; all valid Welch cells satisfy the minimum count requirement. These conclusions are dataset-specific associations and do not imply causality or generalizability.

The validation for H8 does not support the original claim and leads me to reject and close H8. R8 was already only a borderline discovery result: the signed estimate was +0.0231 with interval approximately -0.0001 to 0.0463, and for outcome_012 the approximate 10% relative threshold is about 0.025, so the discovery point estimate was just below the clinically meaningful region and the interval touched zero. The new independent validation R13 has a signed estimate of -0.0047, already in the claimed direction, meaning it actually points away from stronger dependency. Its interval is wide and includes modest positive values, but the replication point is near null and inconsistent with the discovery. Combined, these findings argue that H8 is best interpreted as a nonreplicating borderline association, not a supported clinically meaningful predictor association. No claim is currently accepted. The most promising unresolved active hypotheses remain H3 and H10: H3 has a clinically relevant-looking discovery estimate on outcome_006 but imprecise uncertainty, and H10 is a positive but very wide interaction estimate on outcome_014. Next, I propose refinements that decompose these borderline signals rather than simply re-running them: for H3, test feature_060 main effects within common feature_002 subgroups and test whether feature_050 modifies the feature_060-associated difference; for H10, test feature_052 main effects within feature_002 subgroups to see whether the apparent interaction concentrates in one subgroup. I also register broader screens using common binary markers feature_050, feature_021, and feature_045 on high-variance or less conventional dependency outcomes, including outcome_014, outcome_006, outcome_013, outcome_011, outcome_008, outcome_001, and outcome_016. These are still dataset-specific associational analyses; causal interpretation and generalizability remain unsupported.

No assessments are due because no new evidence has been delivered, and changing a scientific conclusion would require evidence already in the ledger. The active set already includes valuable focused follow-ups for H3 and H10 through H13-H17, plus broad common-marker screens through H18-H24. To preserve feasibility, the new proposals favor well-powered binary predictors: feature_034, feature_002, and feature_060 have roughly half-population prevalence; feature_042, feature_045, feature_027, feature_065, feature_021, and feature_012 are sufficiently common for the 2000-row dataset. These extend outcome coverage to previously untested dependency scores and avoid low-prevalence markers unless a later signal is unusually large. The negative-direction claims hypothesize that the exposed group has stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator score. For standard-scale outcomes centered near -0.25, the clinical reference is about 0.025 in the claimed direction; for outcome_001 it is closer to 0.041; for outcome_014 and outcome_006 the literal 10% of a near-zero mean is unstable, so an absolute shift near 0.02-0.025 will be interpreted cautiously. The linked interaction transfers the active feature_052-by-feature_002 modification from outcome_014 to outcome_006 to test whether the subgroup-specific dependency pattern is shared across related high-variance dependency outcomes or is outcome-specific. These remain associational dataset findings; causal interpretation and generalizability are not assumed.

No assessments are due because no new evidence has arrived since the last synthesis, and there are no claims with direct evidence whose scientific conclusion can be changed now. I will request the 12 untested claims H13-H24 because they are the most informative next batch under the current evidence. H13-H15 decompose the active outcome_006 / feature_060 signal by testing feature_050 as a modifier and testing feature_060 within feature_002 subgroups. H16-H17 decompose the active outcome_014 / feature_052 / feature_002 interaction by testing the subgroup-specific main effects, which is more directly interpretable than relying on a wide interaction estimate. H18-H24 are high-priority common-marker screens across outcomes with larger or less conventional scale: feature_050 on outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_013; feature_021 on outcome_011, outcome_008, and outcome_001; and feature_045 on outcome_016. This keeps cell counts adequate while testing whether the borderline feature_060 and feature_052 signals are isolated or part of a broader measured-marker pattern. The later registered screens H25-H36 remain untested for the next round unless new validation or results change priorities. All requested analyses remain associational dataset-specific comparisons; I will interpret effects against approximate clinically relevant shifts of about 0.025 for standard dependency outcomes, about 0.041 for outcome_001, and cautiously around 0.02-0.025 absolute shift for outcome_014 and outcome_006.

All new Welch cells are valid and satisfy the minimum-count requirement, so the main concerns are multiplicity, subgroup-specific false discovery, and clinical relevance rather than feasibility. I again interpreted the signed estimates so that positive values support the registered claim direction. For standard dependency outcomes centered near -0.25, a clinically relevant shift is about 0.025 in the claimed direction; for outcome_001 it is about 0.041; for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose overall means are near zero, literal relative scaling is unstable, so I used a cautious absolute shift around 0.02-0.025 as a working scientific threshold. None of the new results clears a clinically meaningful interval entirely, so no new claim is accepted. H13 and H17 are rejected because their point estimates are opposite the claimed directions and the results do not indicate a clinically meaningful negative interaction or negative subgroup main effect. H19 is rejected because feature_050 on outcome_006 points away from stronger dependency and the interval excludes clinically meaningful support. H21, H22, H23, and H24 are rejected because feature_021 or feature_045 associations are near null, and their upper confidence limits do not reach the relevant clinical thresholds for outcome_011, outcome_008, outcome_001, and outcome_016. H14, H18, and H20 remain unresolved but deferred: their point estimates are modest and not precise enough to support a conclusion, making immediate follow-up less informative. H15 and H16 remain active because they decompose the two earlier borderline signals in a biologically more interpretable way: H15 is the feature_060 main effect within feature_002=0, with a signed estimate of about +0.031 and an interval that still crosses null and the clinical threshold; H16 is the feature_052 main effect within feature_002=1, with a signed estimate of about +0.028 and a wider interval. These subgroup main effects are more interpretable than the original broad or interaction claims, but they are also at higher risk of multiplicity because they were selected after seeing overall signals. I am validating H15 because it is the strongest refined subgroup-specific signal, has balanced subgroup cell counts, and directly tests whether the outcome_006 feature_060 association is concentrated in a common subgroup. If validation is null, it will downgrade the H3/H15 line; if it replicates a meaningful positive effect, I can reassess a refined claim rather than the diluted original claim. All conclusions remain associational in the supplied dataset and do not imply causality or generalizability. Predictor labels are opaque, so biological mechanism remains speculative.

The validation for H15 is supportive enough to accept the refined subgroup-specific claim in this dataset. The discovery signed estimate was +0.0314, and the independent validation signed estimate was +0.0291, both in the claimed direction, meaning that exposed samples had rawly more negative outcome_006 dependency scores than comparator samples within the feature_002=0 subgroup. For outcome_006 the overall mean is near zero, so a literal 10% relative threshold is unstable; I therefore used a cautious absolute shift of about 0.02-0.025 on the dependency-score scale. The replicated point estimates are roughly 0.03, above that working threshold and also large relative to the overall magnitude of outcome_006. The discovery and validation confidence intervals are wide and include null values, especially the validation interval, which is conservatively widened for the maximum validation budget. Therefore, the accepted conclusion is not a precise magnitude claim; it is a dataset-specific association claim: feature_060 is associated with stronger outcome_006 dependency among samples with feature_002=0, with substantial uncertainty around the exact effect size. This is not evidence of causality, mechanism, or generalizability beyond the supplied data.

This result supersedes the broader H3 overall feature_060 comparison for follow-up because the signal appears concentrated in the feature_002=0 subgroup and is diluted by the weaker H14 feature_002=1 estimate. I therefore leave H3 unresolved but deferred. The feature_052-by-feature_002 interaction H10 is also deferred because H16 is the more interpretable direct subgroup main-effect estimate; H16 remains active and is the best next validation candidate if resources allow. The newly proposed tests follow the two strongest active lines: outcome_014 and outcome_012 feature_060 effects within feature_002=0 test whether the accepted H15 association transfers to a companion dependency outcome or a standard-scale dependency outcome, while outcome_006 feature_052 within feature_002=1 tests whether the feature_052 signal seen for outcome_014 has a companion effect for outcome_006. Next analyses should prioritize these direct subgroup effects and the untested broad screens H25-H31/H33-H35/H36, but I will remain cautious with multiplicity and will not accept subgroup-specific effects unless the point estimates are clinically meaningful and, ideally, directionally replicated.

No assessments are due because no new discovery or validation evidence has been delivered since the H15 validation result. The current primary supported dataset-specific finding is H15: feature_060 is associated with stronger outcome_006 dependency among samples with feature_002=0. The next scientifically useful questions are transfer, specificity, and robustness. The proposed feature_060-by-feature_002 interaction tests for outcome_014 and outcome_012 examine whether the accepted pattern also holds in a companion high-variance dependency outcome and a standard-scale dependency outcome, and whether the feature_060 effect is stronger in the feature_002=0 complement than in the feature_002=1 subgroup. With direction -1, a positive signed estimate would mean the raw interaction contrast is negative, i.e. the feature_060 effect is stronger in feature_002=0. The outcome_004 proposal directly tests transfer of the accepted feature_060 effect within feature_002=0 to another standard-scale dependency score, where a clinically meaningful claimed shift is approximately 0.025-0.026. The outcome_006 feature_050=0 robustness proposal tests whether the accepted association persists after excluding a common predictor with a near-null or opposite prior association for outcome_006; this helps distinguish a feature_060 signal from proxying through feature_050, although it remains an associational robustness check rather than causal identification. The outcome_012 feature_052 proposal tests whether the active feature_052-in-feature_002=1 signal from outcome_014 has a companion effect on a standard-scale outcome. The feature_042 screens for outcome_012 and outcome_004 add a well-powered common binary marker (about 463 exposed, about 1537 comparator) to broaden the predictor-outcome map on outcomes where a meaningful shift is near 0.025. For outcome_006 and outcome_014, because their overall means are near zero, I continue to interpret a roughly 0.02-0.025 absolute shift cautiously rather than relying on an unstable 10% relative denominator. All proposed comparisons remain dataset-specific associations; no causal mechanism or external generalizability is assumed, and predictor labels are opaque.

No scientific conclusion can be changed now because no new evidence has been delivered since H15 was validated and accepted. I am therefore allocating the next 12 analyses to the most informative untested comparisons. The first group tests whether the accepted H15 finding is specific and transferable rather than a narrow subgroup artifact: H43 robustness-checks the accepted outcome_006 feature_060 effect within the feature_002=0 and feature_050=0 cell; H42, H37, and H38 test direct transfer of feature_060 within feature_002=0 to outcome_004, outcome_014, and outcome_012; and H40 and H41 formally test whether the feature_060 association is stronger in the feature_002=0 complement than in feature_002=1 for outcome_014 and outcome_012, respectively. With direction -1, positive signed interaction estimates indicate stronger raw negative dependency associated with feature_060 in feature_002=0 than in feature_002=1. The second group tests the separate active feature_052 line by asking whether the feature_052 effect within feature_002=1 seen for outcome_014 has companion effects on related dependency outcomes: H39 for outcome_006 and H44 for outcome_012. I chose these direct subgroup main effects over the more diffuse interaction estimates because they are easier to interpret clinically and connect directly to the active H16 line. The final group preserves broad exploration of well-powered common binary predictors on previously untested outcomes: H25 tests feature_034 on outcome_005, H26 tests feature_002 on outcome_002, H28 tests feature_027 on outcome_009, and H30 tests feature_065 on outcome_007. I deferred feature_042 and additional feature_021, feature_012, feature_037, and feature_045 screens because either prior near-null evidence reduces their current priority or the current targeted lines are more decision-relevant. For standard dependency scores near -0.25, I will interpret clinically meaningful shifts as roughly 0.025 in the claimed direction; for outcome_001 about 0.041; and for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose means are near zero, I will continue to use cautious absolute shifts of roughly 0.02-0.025 rather than unstable literal relative scaling. All selected analyses are dataset-specific associational tests.

All newly delivered Welch comparisons satisfy the minimum cell-count rule, so the main audit issues are multiplicity, subgroup-specific selection after prior borderline signals, lack of covariate adjustment, and whether the point estimates and confidence limits reach a clinically meaningful difference on the dependency-score scale. I continued interpreting signed estimates so that positive values support the registered claim direction. For outcomes whose overall mean is around -0.25, a 10% relative difference is approximately 0.025. For outcome_001 it is about 0.041. For outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose means are near -0.093, a literal 10% relative threshold is about 0.009, but because the values are negative and near zero I still treat effects near 0.02 to 0.025 cautiously rather than relying solely on unstable relative scaling. The strongest new result is H39, outcome_006 feature_052 versus comparator within feature_002=1: signed estimate +0.0744, 95% CI +0.0190 to +0.1298. It is entirely in the claimed direction and large enough that even the lower bound may exceed a literal 10% threshold for outcome_006. However, it is a subgroup-specific follow-up selected after the feature_052 line, uses an exposed cell of only 190 observations, and is not independent validation. Therefore I leave H39 unresolved and request validation. H37, outcome_014 feature_060 within feature_002=0, is a promising transfer from the accepted H15 line: signed estimate +0.0340, CI -0.0104 to +0.0785. It supports the same direction and reaches a clinically suggestive point magnitude, but the interval still includes null and lower clinical values, so it remains active. H43, the feature_050=0 robustness subset of the accepted feature_060 outcome_006 subgroup, has a consistent point estimate +0.0262 but CI -0.0243 to +0.0767; it is supportive but imprecise and is deferred rather than treated as confirmation. The transfer test to outcome_004, H42, is near null and opposite the claimed direction, signed -0.0061 with upper bound only +0.0159, below the outcome_004 clinical threshold, so it is rejected and closed. The outcome_012 transfer H38 is also very weak: +0.0037, CI -0.0183 to +0.0257. Its upper bound only barely reaches the standard clinical threshold, so I defer rather than accept, but it is low priority. The interaction tests H40 and H41 do not support the registered interaction directions and their upper bounds do not establish meaningful effect modification under my interpretive threshold, so they are rejected/closed; their wide intervals reflect limited precision and interaction coding is less directly interpretable than subgroup main effects. H44, the feature_052 transfer to outcome_012 within feature_002=1, is opposite the claimed direction and has upper bound +0.0187 below the outcome_012 threshold, so it is rejected. The broad screens H26, H28, and H30 are near null or opposite and have upper bounds below their respective clinical thresholds, so they are rejected/closed. H25, feature_034 on outcome_005, is not clinically compelling because the point estimate is only +0.0102, although its upper bound +0.0261 marginally crosses the 0.025 threshold; I therefore defer rather than reject. Overall, the only new candidate strong enough for validation is H39. If validation replicates a clinically meaningful positive estimate, it can be accepted as a separate dataset-specific association; if not, the feature_052 line for outcome_006 should be downgraded and attention can return to H16 and H37. No conclusions here imply causality, mechanism, or generalizability beyond the supplied dataset, and predictor labels are opaque.

The newly delivered validation evidence changes the interpretation of the two active follow-up lines. H8 was already rejected in discovery because the signed estimate was only +0.0231 and the 95% interval included null; its independent validation estimate was in the opposite direction, signed -0.0047 with a wide interval including null. The evidence therefore does not support the claim that feature_005 is associated with stronger outcome_012 dependency in this dataset, and I keep H8 rejected and closed. H24, feature_045 versus comparator on outcome_016, was near null in discovery and remains near null in validation: signed validation estimate +0.0068, interval -0.0212 to +0.0348. Although the validation upper bound can cross the approximate 10% threshold for a standard outcome centered near -0.256, the point estimate is far too small to support a clinically meaningful association. H24 remains rejected and closed. H39 is the most consequential new result. Its discovery estimate was large and entirely in the claimed direction, outcome_006 feature_052 versus comparator within feature_002=1 signed +0.0744 with CI +0.0190 to +0.1298, but the independent validation estimate reversed to signed -0.0208 with a wide interval from -0.1205 to +0.0789. That pattern is inconsistent with a robust dataset-specific association and is most parsimoniously treated as a discovery-stage false positive or an unstable subgroup estimate. I therefore reject and close H39. The failure of H39 weakens the feature_052 line overall, although it does not automatically refute H16 because H16 concerns a different outcome, outcome_014, and remains an independent active claim. The currently supported finding remains H15: within the supplied dataset, feature_060 is associated with stronger outcome_006 dependency among samples with feature_002=0, with discovery signed +0.0314 and validation signed +0.0291. This is accepted as an associational, dataset-specific finding with imprecise magnitude, not as causal evidence or a generalizable biological claim. The strongest unresolved candidates now are H37, outcome_014 feature_060 within feature_002=0 signed +0.0340 with CI -0.0104 to +0.0785, and H16, outcome_014 feature_052 within feature_002=1 signed +0.0284 with CI -0.0252 to +0.0820. Both have point estimates above my cautious 0.02 to 0.025 absolute threshold for these near-zero-centered outcomes, but both confidence intervals include null or opposite-direction values. If validation resources are available in the next appraise stage, H37 is the more informative validation target because it tests whether the accepted feature_060 pattern transfers from outcome_006 to the companion outcome outcome_014 within the same informative subgroup. H16 is secondary because the related feature_052/outcome_006 validation failure reduces confidence in the feature_052 line. The newly registered proposals aim to clarify these lines without overcommitting to subgroup artifacts: a global outcome_014 feature_052 test checks whether the H16 signal is broad or restricted; a feature_002=1 feature_060 test for outcome_014 provides the complement of H37; a feature_050=1 robustness check within the accepted H15 subgroup tests whether the accepted outcome_006 feature_060 pattern persists outside the feature_050=0 cell; and a global outcome_010 feature_060 screen tests whether the accepted predictor has a broader standard-scale dependency effect. All conclusions remain associational and dataset-specific, and predictor labels remain opaque.

No assessments are due. The corrected proposal form avoids linked refinements that lack available motivating evidence. The scientifically motivated first group tests whether the accepted dataset-specific finding, stronger outcome_006 dependency with feature_060 in the feature_002=0 subgroup, has breadth or specificity beyond that exact outcome-subgroup comparison. A global outcome_014 feature_060 comparison tests whether the effect remains visible when averaging over feature_002 strata; a feature_002=0 outcome_010 feature_060 comparison tests transfer to another standard-scale dependency outcome within the previously informative subgroup; and an outcome_006 feature_060 comparison restricted to feature_002=0 and feature_052=0 tests robustness against the false-positive feature_052 lead. The remaining proposals broaden the predictor-outcome map using well-powered binary markers and one previously validated categorical predictor. feature_042 is tested on outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_008; feature_034 is tested on outcome_006 and outcome_012, with the outcome_012 test motivated by the borderline feature_034 signal on outcome_005; and feature_054 level_001 versus level_002 is tested on outcome_014 and outcome_012 to include a nonbinary predictor type. Direction -1 encodes the hypothesis that exposed groups have rawly more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. For standard dependency scores near a mean of about -0.25, I will treat roughly 0.025 as clinically meaningful; for outcome_001 roughly 0.041; for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose means are near zero, I will use cautious absolute shifts around 0.02 to 0.025 rather than an unstable literal relative threshold. These remain associational, dataset-specific comparisons and do not imply causality, mechanism, or external generalizability.

No assessments are due because no new discovery or validation evidence has arrived since the last synthesis. I selected only untested claim references, so these analyses request new samples rather than reusing cached evidence. The first seven selections concentrate on the currently supported feature_060 association with stronger outcome_006 dependency within feature_002=0. H53 and H49 test robustness inside the accepted feature_002=0 subgroup after restricting to feature_052=0 or feature_050=1, respectively, helping determine whether the accepted effect is stable across relevant correlated predictors. H51, H48, and the existing H37 together map outcome_014 feature_060 overall and in both feature_002 strata, clarifying whether the feature_060 pattern transfers to the companion high-variance outcome and is subgroup-specific or broader. H50 and H52 test standard-scale outcome_010 overall and within feature_002=0, providing direct transfer screens for the accepted predictor. H47 tests global outcome_014 feature_052, checking whether the active but unvalidated H16 subgroup signal has broader support or remains narrow. The remaining selections preserve broad exploration using well-powered markers: feature_042 on outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_010, and feature_034 on outcome_012 and outcome_006. These broaden the predictor-outcome map without prioritizing predictors that already have replicated null or reversed validation evidence. I will interpret positive signed estimates as supporting the registered hypothesis. For outcomes centered near -0.25, I will treat roughly 0.025 as clinically meaningful; for outcome_001 roughly 0.041; for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose means are near zero, I will use cautious absolute shifts of about 0.02 to 0.025 rather than an unstable literal relative threshold. Discovery CIs alone will not justify acceptance for subgroup-selected claims when prior validation behavior suggests false-positive risk. All interpretations remain associational and dataset-specific.

All new Welch comparisons satisfy the cell-count rule. I again use positive signed estimates to support the registered direction, with a practical threshold around 0.025 for standard outcomes such as outcome_010 and outcome_012, about 0.041 for outcome_001, and about 0.025 for the near-zero-centered outcomes outcome_006 and outcome_014. The strongest new result is H54, global outcome_014 feature_042: signed estimate +0.0351, 95% CI -0.0012 to +0.0714. Its point magnitude exceeds my clinical threshold and its interval barely includes null, making it the best independent-validation candidate because it is a broad, well-powered screen rather than a post-hoc subgroup refinement. I therefore request validation for H54. H53, outcome_006 feature_060 within feature_002=0 and feature_052=0, is also promising (+0.0487, CI -0.0007 to +0.0981) and supports robustness of the accepted H15 pattern after excluding the false-positive feature_052 subgroup. However, H53 is a nested refinement of an already accepted claim and has not yet received independent validation, so I keep it active but do not validate it ahead of H54. H49 gives a similar point (+0.0512) but has only 103 and 106 observations, so its interval is too wide; it is deferred as supportive but unstable. H37 remains active as a candidate transfer of feature_060 to outcome_014 within feature_002=0, but its lower interval bound is less favorable than H54's. The new complement and transfer screens mostly weaken broader or related interpretations. H51 global outcome_014 feature_060 is near null (+0.0063), H48 outcome_014 feature_060 within feature_002=1 is opposite and below the claimed positive threshold (-0.0220, CI upper +0.0236), H50 global outcome_010 feature_060 is near null and opposite (-0.0027, upper below 0.025), and H52 outcome_010 feature_060 within feature_002=0 is clinically weak (+0.0116). These patterns are consistent with the accepted feature_060 association being specific rather than a broad dependency predictor, but I defer rather than reject the few comparisons whose intervals still permit meaningful positive effects. The feature_052 line is downgraded: H47 global outcome_014 feature_052 is near null (+0.0066), H39 already failed validation for outcome_006, and H16's subgroup effect remains unreplicated, so H16 is deferred. The feature_042 screen is mixed: H54 is promising, H55 outcome_006 is weak, and H29 outcome_010 is opposite and below the clinical threshold, so only H54 receives validation while H55 is deferred and H29 is closed. feature_034 remains unconvincing: H58 is clinically negligible, H57 is near-null/opposite, and H25 remains a deferred borderline lead. No accepted finding changes yet. Validation will determine whether H54 becomes a separate dataset-specific association. All conclusions remain associational and dataset-specific, with no implication of causality, mechanism, or external generalizability.

The validation response for H15 closes the main question about the currently supported association. The independent validation estimate for outcome_006 feature_060 versus comparator within feature_002=0 is signed +0.0291, close to the discovery estimate of +0.0314 and in the same claimed direction. Both point estimates exceed my practical threshold for this near-zero-centered outcome, although the validation interval is wide and includes null and clinically borderline values. That uncertainty argues against strong magnitude claims, but the directional replication is informative: it makes a pure discovery-stage false positive less parsimonious. I therefore keep H15 accepted and closed as a dataset-specific associational finding: within the supplied dataset, feature_060=1 is associated with a more negative outcome_006 dependency score than feature_060=0 among samples with feature_002=0. This is not evidence of causality, mechanism, or external generalizability. No other claim is newly accepted. H54 remains the strongest pending candidate: global outcome_014 feature_042 has signed estimate +0.0351 with a 95% interval of -0.0012 to +0.0714. It is clinically suggestive and nearly excludes null, but it is still discovery-only, and its pending independent validation should determine acceptance or rejection. H53, the feature_052=0 subset of the accepted feature_060/outcome_006/feature_002=0 subgroup, has signed estimate +0.0487 and interval -0.0007 to +0.0981; it is supportive of the accepted finding being robust to excluding the false-positive feature_052 lead, but its interval is too imprecise for acceptance. H37, outcome_014 feature_060 within feature_002=0, is a transfer test with signed estimate +0.0340 and interval -0.0104 to +0.0785; it remains active but unresolved. Several negative results are important. H39 had a strong discovery estimate but reversed in validation, so it is closed as an unstable or false-positive subgroup effect. H8 and H24 remain closed after validation showed no clinically meaningful replication. Broad null or opposite results include many feature_060 transfer screens, feature_042/outcome_010, feature_034 screens, feature_052/outcome_012 within feature_002=1, and other near-null binary-marker tests. These negative findings suggest that the accepted feature_060 effect is specific rather than a broad dependency predictor, and they downweight related feature_052 claims. The most informative next analyses are: complete the feature_042 specificity panel around H54, including registered outcome_008/outcome_001/outcome_012/outcome_004 and subgroup tests plus newly registered outcome_009/outcome_015/outcome_013; complete feature_060 specificity with registered H63 and small-cell robustness H49; and broaden the predictor map using feature_011, feature_007, feature_035, and feature_022 on informative high-variance and standard-scale outcomes. Pending validation of H54 is the single most decisive result, followed by whether feature_042 effects replicate on other outcomes or whether they appear confined to outcome_014. For the accepted H15 line, validation or further robustness would be useful, but I will not accept nested subgroup refinements unless they are clinically strong, well-powered, or independently replicated.

No assessments are due. The new proposals focus on three scientific questions. First, they test the boundary of the only accepted finding, H15: feature_060 is associated with stronger outcome_006 dependency within feature_002=0. I split the informative feature_002=0 population by feature_034 to ask whether that association persists in both feature_034 strata or is confined to one common marker. I also transfer the accepted predictor to outcome_008 within feature_002=0 to test whether the feature_060 association is outcome-specific or reaches a related high-variance dependency score. Second, while H54 validation is pending, I register a specificity panel for feature_042 on outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_007, and outcome_011. If feature_042 validates for outcome_014, these outcomes will show whether it is a broad dependency marker or specific to outcome_014; if it fails validation, the panel also reduces overinterpretation of the discovery estimate. Third, I add well-powered exploratory screens using categorical feature_054 and binary feature_047, both with sufficient sample sizes, to broaden the predictor-outcome map beyond already heavily probed markers. Direction -1 encodes stronger dependency in the exposed group. No assessments are due. No assessments are due because no new evidence has arrived since the last synthesis. Twelve new discovery results are due. I interpret positive signed mean-difference estimates for direction -1 as stronger dependency in the exposed group, and positive signed estimates for direction +1 as weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interaction claims with direction -1, positive signed output means the exposed-comparator contrast is more negative in the claimed subgroup than in its complement.

The accepted H15 pattern remains that feature_060=1 is associated with more negative outcome_006 scores than feature_060=0 within feature_002=0. The main new substantive signal is H94, global outcome_006 feature_020 exposed=1 versus comparator=0 with registered stronger-dependency direction -1. The signed estimate is -0.0595, CI -0.1043 to -0.0148. Because the interval excludes zero on the opposite side of the registered hypothesis, H94 is rejected as a stronger-dependency association. Other feature_020 screens fail to support a broad stronger-dependency pattern: H93 on outcome_014 is near null (+0.0066, CI -0.0358 to +0.0489) and H95 on outcome_011 is small and opposite the registered stronger direction (-0.0059, CI -0.0349 to +0.0230). feature_047 screens are weak and closed: H83 outcome_014 (+0.0122, CI -0.0277 to +0.0521), H84 outcome_006 (+0.0149, CI -0.0273 to +0.0571), and H85 outcome_011 (+0.0041, CI -0.0246 to +0.0328) do not provide statistically established clinically meaningful differences. The delivered validations are decisive for the pending feature_042 and feature_052/feature_060 boundary questions, and both are negative for the claims as registered. The point estimate is large relative to the outcome_006 scale, but because this is a reversal based on the same discovery sample and no independent validation exists yet, I keep it active unresolved rather than accept it immediately. The next analysis priority is the feature_020 specificity panel, including the newly proposed outcome_015 addition. If those main-effect screens show a coherent outcome_006-specific weak-dependency pattern and later validation of H96 supports it, H96 could become the second accepted finding. If the panel is null or opposite, H96 should be downgraded or closed. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associational statements, subject to confounding and multiple-testing error.

No assessments are due. The accepted set remains H15 only. The cell counts should still be adequate if feature_020 and the stratifying variables are not too strongly associated; if not, the controller can treat it as low-power rather than informative.

These proposals are intended to complement, not replace, the already registered feature_020 specificity panel across the other outcomes. No assessments are due. No assessments are due. All due comparisons H117-H126 test feature_060=1 versus feature_060=0 within feature_002=0 for outcomes other than the already examined feature_002=0 outcomes.
